irac.issue: Whether the impugned levy on tea estates is a tax on lands within the meaning of Entry 49, List II of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution or a tax on despatches of tea, which would be within the competence of the Parliament.
irac.rule: The doctrine of pith and substance, which requires that the true nature and character of the impugned legislation be ascertained to determine its validity. The rule that there is no overlapping of taxes, as a tax on a manufacturer in respect of his goods and a tax on a vendor in respect of his sales are separate and distinct imposts.
irac.application: The impugned levy, in substance, is a levy on despatches of tea and not on tea estates. The levy was held to be violative of Article 301 of the Constitution as it did not have a reasonable nexus with the subject matter of taxation, namely, tea estates.
irac.conclusion: The impugned levy is a tax on despatches of tea and not a tax on lands, and as such, it is outside the competence of the State Legislature.

retrieved_chunks.text: The learned Judges rejected the argument that the mode of levy was merely a measure of the tax. They pointed out further that the quality of tea produced in all tea estates in the State was hot uniform and that the benefit of exemption of reduction in levy has no relation to the need of a particular tea estate for exemption from the levy. The learner Judges concluded "when the provisions before us are examined in their totality, we find no such relationship or nexus between the tea estate and the varied treatment accorded in respect of despatches of different kinds of lea. It seems to us that having regard to all the relevant provision of the statute, including Section 4(2)(aa) and Section 4(4) in substance the impugned levy is a levy in respect of despatches of tea and not in respect of tea estates." Accordingly, the levy was held to be violative of Article 301 of the Constitution. The learned Judges then proceeded to consider the question of legislative competence and held that if the levy is, in substance, on despatches of tea, it cannot be held to be tax on lands.
